# T2. Integer Variables & Adding a Constraint

<!-- section:scenario -->
> **Optional Tutorial (excluded from the 0/100 score)**: Skip anytime once you understand variable types and constraints.

Pack integer quantities `counts[i]` of $n$ item types into a bag with weight limit `maxWeight`, maximizing total value while respecting `0 <= counts[i] <= maxCounts[i]`.

Right now the starter code has **two intentional gaps**:
1. It forgets the weight limit constraint (`sum(weight[i] * counts[i]) <= maxWeight`), so running it immediately triggers a **VIOLATION**.
2. Notice the items must be packed in **integer** units (`counts[i]` cannot be fractional!). Check the variable constructor too (`continuous` vs `integer` in WaSHI, `addVariables` vs `addIntegrals` in `highspy`).

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input**: `maxWeight: number`, `weights: number[]`, `values: number[]`, `maxCounts: number[]`
- **Output**: `{ counts: number[], totalValue: number }` (where every `counts[i]` is an integer)

<!-- section:example -->
With `maxWeight = 10`, `weights = [3, 4, 2]`, `values = [40, 55, 22]`, `maxCounts = [2, 2, 3]`, packing `counts = [2, 1, 0]` weighs $2\times 3 + 1\times 4 = 10$ for maximum integer value **`135`**.

<!-- section:hint1 -->
- **WaSHI**: Declare integer arrays with `m.integer(n, { lb: 0, ub: (i) => input.maxCounts[i] })` (or a loop of `m.integer(...)`) and add the weight limit using `expr\`dot(${input.weights}, ${counts}) <= ${input.maxWeight}\``.
- **highspy**: Use `[h.addIntegral(lb=0, ub=m) for m in input_data["maxCounts"]]` and add `h.addConstr(h.qsum(w * x for w, x in zip(weights, counts)) <= max_weight)`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Without the integer requirement (`continuous`), packing `counts = [2, 1, 0]` vs `[0, 2, 1]` behaves differently — in general, fractional LP relaxations can achieve strictly higher objective values than physically possible integer items! Remember `Math.round(...)` when extracting integer solutions if solver tolerance leaves `1.999999999`.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} v_i x_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} w_i x_i \le W_{\max} \\
& x_i \in \{0, 1, \dots, u_i\} \quad \forall i
\end{aligned}
$$
